findings.finding: uvicorn.access is disabled on two factually false premises, when routing it through the JSON root handler (the treatment uvicorn.error already gets) demonstrably yields a valid JSON line carrying the correct request_id. disabled=True permanently drops client address, HTTP version and query string from the operational record and suppresses any future uvicorn.access WARNING/ERROR.
findings.suggestion: Move "uvicorn.access" from _SILENCED_LOGGERS to _JSON_ROUTED_LOGGERS and correct the comment.

findings.finding: The RED counter is labelled with the raw request path, not the matched route template, and _request_counts is a module-level Counter that never evicts. 150 unauthenticated requests to distinct nonexistent paths produced 154 series and a 10302-byte /metrics response. Unbounded attacker-driven memory growth and metric-cardinality explosion on an unauthenticated endpoint the runtime-SLO sensor scrapes.
findings.suggestion: Label with the matched route (scope["route"].path) or bucket unmatched paths to a single __unmatched__ label.

findings.finding: Inbound X-Request-ID is accepted with no length or charset validation. An 8000-character value was reflected verbatim into the response header and written at full length into every log line. Not injection (log forging and CRLF splitting both verified blocked), but unbounded attacker-controlled data written to the log sink E15-S1 exists to protect.
findings.suggestion: Accept the inbound id only if it matches an opaque-token shape such as ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$, else generate one.

findings.finding: register_sensitive silently ignores any value shorter than _MIN_REDACTABLE_LENGTH (6). _scrub('secret=AB123 here', ['AB123']) returns the string unchanged. A caller registering a short identifier gets no signal that it is unprotected.
findings.suggestion: Log a warning, or raise, when a registered value falls below the threshold.

findings.finding: The AC2 oracle is a boot-time snapshot that decays. 9/9 loggers carry a RedactionFilter at configure_logging time; two loggers created afterwards carry 0. Redaction still holds via the root handler filter, so AC1 is safe today. Forward risk: a later story adding propagate=False plus its own handler - exactly what uvicorn does - bypasses the only load-bearing filter.
findings.suggestion: Install the filter via a logging.setLoggerClass hook, or assert the invariant at request time rather than once at boot.

findings.finding: _scrub is O(registered values x text length) per log line. 200 registered values against a 4000-char line costs 23.7 ms of CPU for one line. No group-A caller registers anything, but the project SLO is p95_ms 500.
findings.suggestion: Consider a single combined alternation pattern, or cap the number of registered values per request.

findings.finding: AC1's literal subject - 'when a schedule is computed from each triple' - does not exist in group A; it is verified by proxy on Money arithmetic over 200 random triples. The test file discloses this, and it parallels the contract retargeting in the context pack section 3, so it is a defensible narrowing - but AC1 is not closed as worded until the schedule generator lands.
findings.suggestion: Re-assert AC1 against the real schedule generator when E9-S3 lands.
